## Annotation

Fayerman reports Walt Lawrence’s account that a group of five or six people at George Pearson Hospital wanted to direct their own care; that in the early 1980s the Canadian Paraplegic Association (now SCI BC) helped with a cost analysis; that Lawrence credits then-MLA Doug Mowat with championing the cause; that a study found community living about 30 percent less expensive than the rehabilitation facility; and that in 1985 Lawrence and friends moved into “a co-op housing cluster called the Creekview Co-operative Apartment near Granville Island.”

The “30 percent less expensive” figure does not match Norman Haw’s 1989 summary of a 1987 evaluation (about 60% of Pearson costs). Both statements are catalogued. They are not collapsed into one finding.

This article does not mention CSIL or ECPM.

## Open questions

- Whether the “cost analysis” is the 1987 evaluation, an earlier CPA study, or something else.
- Exact legal name of the co-op in 1985.
